I should have asked those questions sooner. Here's why I couldn't, and what they're about.

**Why they never reached you.** When plumb's judge needs your answer, it files the question in the folder of the session that was running at the time. Each session can only ask the questions in its own folder. My session had one, the study-room question, and I asked it. The other 103 sit in eight other sessions' folders, several from sessions that ended between 17 and 19 October. Nothing moves a dead session's questions to a live one, so they wait forever and quietly hold every merge. That's a bug in plumb, and I've added it to the board.

**What they're about.** The merge check printed only the first ten titles. They fall into three groups, and many of the 103 repeat the same record:
- **Merge holds:** which requirements need their proof shown and confirmed, whether the test, question and proof holds apply to merges into work branches, and the rule that a merge is never green while an affected acceptance test lacks a passing run.
- **The background refresh:** refreshing only what's out of date, and the refresh running tests on another session's branch.
- **plumb-85's own records:** issue routing through the question tool (INT-099), and whether your own answer settles the question it answers.

**Proposed fix.** `clarify --wait` in any live session also hands over questions left in ended sessions' folders, oldest first, a few at a time, and I ask them through the question tool. Say "go" for that and I'll build it on a branch.

**Tests.** I merged main into `intent/issue-routing` with no conflicts. plumb is now running every test that covers the branch's 150 changed files, on the merged code, under the heavy lock. It's not the full suite. Nothing lands until they all pass. If any fail, I fix them first.

**Also queued:** your answer that a proof confirmation follows its record through a renumber. That's a small change to `proof.owner_confirmed`. I'll make it after the landings, so it doesn't touch code mid-merge.
